Fashion changes with social, technological and material conditions. Clothing reflects the circumstances and values of its time.
Industrialisation supported sewing-machine use and ready-to-wear production. Technology changed how garments could be manufactured and sold.
Historical features can reappear in contemporary fashion. Designers reinterpret silhouettes, details or materials for a new context.

Styling, material quality, price and marketing shape a designer's image. These decisions communicate position and target market.
Haute couture is custom made for private clients. It uses made-to-order design, fittings and specialist production.
Ready-to-wear is produced in sizes for retail sale. Customers can select from prepared styles and take the garment home.
